ModelValidatorExternal.release_notes:
### PSSE Dynamics

- **New: Automatic Detection and Repair of Missing PLB Dynamics Models.** A PSSE test whose event requires a PLB-driven disturbance could previously run to completion and report success even though its selected DYR file had no active PLB model - silently producing a flat, event-less result. The app now checks for this at run time: if the selected DYR lacks an active PLB model, it automatically switches to a sibling DYR that has one, or - if none exists - generates one from an active GENCLS model in the case. Auto-generated files are clearly logged as not human-authored and should be reviewed before trusting compliance results that depend on them.

### Report Generation

- **Figure Captions and "Fig." Bookmarks Removed Under TocMode "None"/"Simple".** Every plot page previously printed a "Fig:X.Y TestID:..." caption and added a matching nested "Fig." bookmark, regardless of TocMode - redundant once each test already has its own unique TestID and a descriptive bookmark. These are now only generated under TocMode "Figures" or "Both", which actually build a List of Figures from them.
- **Report Header Line Breaks Are Now Preserved.** A multi-line Header (e.g. company name, project name, and study type typed on separate lines in the report config) was previously re-flowed into wrapped lines by width, discarding the line breaks you typed. Explicit line breaks are now preserved exactly as entered, in both PDF and Word reports.
- **Test Suite Name No Longer Printed on the First Plot Page Under TocMode "None".** Since the descriptive bookmarks already identify each test, the Test Suite Name heading is now omitted from the first page of each scenario when TocMode is "None".
- **Fixed: Plot Position Could Shift Between Pages Depending on Which Headings Were Shown.** The plot grid's position and size previously depended on whether the Title/Test Suite heading happened to be drawn on that particular page (e.g. suppressed under TocMode "None", or already shown earlier in a multi-page scenario). The space for these headings is now always reserved identically whether or not the text is actually drawn, so every plot sits at the same position and scale across all pages when scrolling through a report.
